Here's your Monday news rundown. Grab a coffee, it's a wild one.

**Money Talk**
- **Saudi investor conference spooked by Houthi attacks.**
  The Kingdom's big 2026 investor conference is off until 2027, thanks to ongoing Houthi missile and drone volleys. Hard to pitch stability when explosions are hitting your airports, huh? [S4]
- **Apple's iPhone Duo making Jim Cramer look smart (for once).**
  Preorders for the new iPhone Duo are reportedly through the roof, proving that if you put enough shiny new tech in people's hands, they'll open their wallets. Cramer called it, and now he'll probably remind us for a month straight. [S3]
- **French protests spark debt sell-off, investors get cold feet.**
  Violent protests over the weekend, with public buildings torched and shops looted, have spooked the markets. France is seeing a fresh wave of bond and stock selling, widening the gap between French and German borrowing costs. Pas bon. [S15]
- **Home sellers are desperate, cutting prices at 15-year high.**
  If you're looking to buy, now might be your moment. More than 3,000 properties *a day* are seeing asking price cuts, a level not seen in 15 years. Everyone's getting cooked in this market, except maybe cash buyers. [S9]
- **SCOTUS might legalize moonshine for home distillers.**
  The Supreme Court is taking up a 160-year-old ban on home distilling, meaning you could soon legally make your own whiskey in the garage. Talk about a potential new cottage industry, or at least some wilder parties. [S16]

**World Lore**
- **Australia's PM calls lawmaker's critical injury "no accident."**
  An Australian federal lawmaker was critically injured after being hit by a car, and the Prime Minister straight-up said it wasn't an accident. Driver arrested, but the implications are chilling. [S21]
- **France in chaos, Macron condemns violent protests.**
  Macron is speaking out as violent protests across France lead to thousands of arrests and widespread looting. This isn't just about domestic politics; it's rattling investors and causing a debt sell-off. [S15][S22]
- **Ukraine, Russia trade blows; Trump-Zelenskyy relations sour.**
  More of the same on the front lines, with Ukraine launching drone strikes and Russia hitting back with deadly attacks. Meanwhile, the political drama between Trump and Zelenskyy is apparently getting spicy. [S23]
- **Alberta eyes independence, but probably just for leverage.**
  Voters in Canada's oil-rich Alberta are deciding whether to take a step towards an independence referendum. Analysts don't think they'll actually break away, but it's a clear play for more power against Mark Carney's government. [S25][S33]
- **Houthi attacks escalate, kill 50 at Yemen military camp.**
  Iran-backed Houthi militants claimed responsibility for a deadly strike on a Yemeni government military camp, killing at least 50 new recruits. This follows earlier attacks on Saudi Arabia and signals a serious regional uptick in violence. [S4][S35]

**Tech Tea**
- **Apple's "Pro and tell" event hints at touchscreen MacBook.**
  Mark your calendars: Apple's got another product launch next week. Analysts are buzzing about a touchscreen MacBook Pro with an OLED display and a refreshed iPad Mini. Take my money, I guess. [S2][S46]
- **AI assistant startup "Town" hits unicorn status in four months.**
  An AI assistant company just bagged a $108 million Series B, pushing it to a unicorn valuation just four months after launching. The AI gold rush is still in full swing, apparently. [S41]
- **People are using AI to "dumb down" their smart TVs.**
  This is peak tech irony: folks are so fed up with ads and bloatware on their smart TVs that they're deploying AI agents to strip it all out and regain control. Who needs "smart" when you just want a TV? [S44]
- **Ukraine pulls off first-ever drone evacuation of wounded soldier.**
  In a grim but innovative first, Ukraine used an aerial drone to evacuate a wounded soldier from the frontline. The future of battlefield medicine just got a lot more robotic. [S39]
- **European telcos gang up to challenge Starlink.**
  Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica, and Vodafone are teaming up to launch their own direct-to-device satellite program. They're trying to build a European alternative to SpaceX's Starlink. Competition is good, right? [S50]

**Creator Szn**
- **Vinted blocks looters from hawking stolen goods.**
  In France, after a weekend of violent protests and looting, resale platform Vinted had to step in and block people trying to sell off stolen items. Definitely not the kind of "haul" content they want. [S6]
- **Amazon leverages Thursday Night Football for ad cash.**
  TNF is Amazon Prime Video's crown jewel, and they're using it to reel in ad dollars from both traditional sports advertisers and wider media budgets. Streaming sports is a whole new ball game for Madison Avenue. [S56]
- **Target goes after TikTok trends for home decor revamp.**
  The big-box retailer is leaning into buzzy TikTok brands like "Mellow Sleep" to overhaul its home category. Looks like retailers are finally realizing where the youth are getting their aesthetic inspo. [S58]
- **The Verge pivots audience strategy for "Google Zero."**
  News pubs are prepping for Google's next big algorithm shift. The Verge is restructuring its audience team to focus on loyal readers over chasing fleeting traffic. Smart move for long-term survival. [S57]
- **Nathan Fielder gets a surprise call from Elizabeth Holmes.**
  This one's wild: Nathan Fielder, of "The Rehearsal" fame, had Elizabeth Holmes call him for a WIRED interview, where she apparently told him, "I trust you." The intersection of true crime, tech drama, and cringe comedy is truly something. [S53]

**Speed Round**
- Elon Musk says he'll give a SpaceX share to every child in America next year, details TBD.
- An alleged Saudi spy was caught bugging OpenAI HQ, and feds are worried about national security.
- North Sea oil rig workers are planning strikes, threatening UK fuel supplies.
- Amazon is funding 12 small nuclear reactors at a former Indiana coal plant.
- WhatsApp accidentally leaked internal instructions for its Meta chatbot, including "WHAT NOT TO SAY."
- Trump adviser Ric Grenell is accused of a "pay-for-influence" offer to a Turkish billionaire for access to "POTUS."
- Xbox's new Disc-to-Digital program lets you convert physical games, but don't dump your collection just yet.
